sourceIssues.locator: Corollary 2.8 and its proof, pp.499–500, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 184 (2016), 487–526 (publisher PDF, SHA-256 3425f269…40e2)
sourceIssues.printed: For p > 0, the source asserts the existence of nonnegative integers λ and t satisfying 0 < λ ≤ v², with |disc(NS(X))| = p^t λ |disc(NS(M_H(v)))|. Its proof uses a natural lattice injection Zv ⊕ (v^⊥ ∩ N(X)) ↪ N(X) with torsion cokernel, states the discriminant of Zv ⊕ v^⊥ as v² disc(v^⊥ ∩ N(X)), and deduces |disc(N(X))| ≤ v² |disc(v^⊥ ∩ N(X))| by the same argument.
sourceIssues.correction: λ need not be an integer. With I = [N(X) : Zv ⊕ (v^⊥ ∩ N(X))], one has |disc NS(X)| = p^t (v²/I²) |disc NS(M_H(v))| with t ≥ 0. So λ = v²/I² is a positive rational number with λ ≤ v², and I divides v² because v is primitive. For p ∤ v², for example v² = 2 and p ≥ 3 as in the applications, λ is still a p-adic unit, which is what the later arguments use.
sourceIssues.reason: Take v = (1, 0, −1), the Mukai vector of ideal sheaves of length-two subschemes, so M_H(v) = X^[2]. It satisfies condition (C): it is primitive, of rank 1, v² = 2, and gcd(1, 0, −1) = 1. Then v^⊥ ∩ N(X) = NS(X) ⊕ Z(1, 0, 1) with (1, 0, 1)² = −2, so |disc(v^⊥ ∩ N(X))| = 2|disc NS(X)|. The proof's first step gives |disc(v^⊥ ∩ N(X))| = p^r |disc NS(M_H(v))|. Hence |disc NS(X)| = ½ p^r |disc NS(M_H(v))|, which is not of the form p^t λ with λ a positive integer when p is odd. The proof passes from the equality disc(Zv ⊕ K) = I² disc N(X) to an integer multiplier without controlling I, here I = 2. The inequality stated for p = 0 is correct. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction (items 34–35).

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 2.9, p.500, as used in the proof of Theorem 2.10, p.503, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 184 (2016), 487–526 (publisher PDF, SHA-256 3425f269…40e2)
sourceIssues.printed: Proposition 2.9 takes d positive and Λ ⊂ Λ_2d positive definite of rank 2. It asserts that some positive N and nonzero a, b give a primitive embedding of Λ into Λ_2md for every positive m with (i) m = 1[N] and (ii) m prime to a and b, both quadratic residues modulo m. The proof represents Λ's primitive embedding into Λ_2d by a tuple (V, W, γ, t).
sourceIssues.correction: Assume Λ is a primitive sublattice of Λ_2d. In the proof of Theorem 2.10, choose the lattice Λ containing v, w with v² = 2, v·w = 1 to be primitive. For example, in Λ_2d = ⟨2d⟩ ⊕ U with basis h, e, f, take the span of v = e + f and w = kh + e. It is primitive, since (x, y, z) ↦ (z, y − z) retracts it, and its Gram matrix [[2, 1], [1, 2dk²]] is positive definite.
sourceIssues.reason: The proof starts from a primitive embedding Λ ⊂ Λ_2d, which the statement does not provide, and the statement fails for non-primitive Λ. In Λ_2 = ⟨2⟩ ⊕ U, the sublattice Λ generated by 2h and 2(e + f) has Gram matrix diag(8, 8). Take m = 1, which satisfies (i) and (ii) for every N, a, b. A primitive embedding of Λ into Λ_2 would give a 2-dimensional subspace of Λ_2/2Λ_2 = F_2³ on which the half-norm Q(x, y, z) = x² + yz vanishes, since Λ has all half-norms even. The nonzero zeros of Q are (0,0,1), (0,1,0) and (1,1,1), and each pairwise sum has Q = 1, so no such plane exists. Noted by the extraction (items 38–41), which also gave the primitive choice above.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.1, p.506, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 184 (2016), 487–526 (publisher PDF, SHA-256 3425f269…40e2)
sourceIssues.printed: The proof invokes Riemann-Roch to assert surjectivity of H⁰(C, 3L|_C) → 3L|_C/(3L|_C − D(p) − D(q)) for every p and q under consideration. It assigns to 3L|_C − D(p) − D(q) the degree 3r − 4 > r = deg(ω_{C/k}), observing that evenness of r implies r > 1.
sourceIssues.correction: Pass to 2L before this step, as the proof already allows ("up to replacing L by 2L"), so that r = L² ≥ 4 and 3r − 4 > r holds.
sourceIssues.reason: 3r − 4 > r holds only for r > 2. "r is even, so that r > 1" leaves r = 2, the double-plane case, where 3r − 4 = r and the surjectivity argument as written does not apply. The proposition only claims the existence of some L′ with bounded invariants, so doubling L is allowed. Noted by the extraction (item 50), which also leaves the characteristic-two nonreduced-curve argument as an open check.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 3.17, p.517, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 184 (2016), 487–526 (publisher PDF, SHA-256 3425f269…40e2)
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts that some positive N and nonzero a, b yield a finite set of polarized K3 surfaces (X, H) that are nonsuperspecial, over k, of degree 2md. Here m is positive with (i) m = 1[N], (ii) m coprime to a and b, both quadratic residues modulo m, and (iii) the discriminant of NS(X_k̄) has p-adic valuation bounded by t_0.
sourceIssues.correction: There are only finitely many k-isomorphism classes of nonsuperspecial K3 surfaces X over k admitting a polarization H of such a degree 2md with (i)–(iii). The polarized pairs themselves need not be finite in number.
sourceIssues.reason: On a fixed eligible (X, H) of degree 2m_0 d, the line bundles H^{⊗ℓ^j} have degree 2(ℓ^{2j} m_0)d. Choose a prime ℓ with a and b quadratic residues modulo ℓ and prime to N, a and b, and let j run through multiples of the order of ℓ² modulo N. Then m = ℓ^{2j} m_0 satisfies (i) and (ii), and (iii) is unchanged. This gives infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic polarized pairs on one surface; the paper does not require polarizations to be primitive. The proof bounds NS(X_k̄) and then the surfaces. The only use, the proof of Theorem 1.3 on p.523, reads "there exist only finitely many K3 surfaces over k", so the corrected statement is what is used. Noted by the extraction (items 88–89).

sourceIssues.locator: §4.1, the definition of N_{α/r}(X) and (4.1), pp.518–519, in the published version, Annals of Mathematics 184 (2016), 487–526 (publisher PDF, SHA-256 3425f269…40e2)
sourceIssues.printed: The source defines N_{α/r}(X) as the inverse image of N(X) under T_{−α/r}, identifies it with the group called CH_{α/r}(X, Z) in [LMS14], and cites [LMS14, Lemma 3.3.3] for (4.1) N_{α/r}(X) = {(ar, D + aα, cω) | a, c ∈ Z, D ∈ NS(X)}.
sourceIssues.correction: Define N_{α/r}(X) directly as the lattice (4.1), the twisted Mukai lattice CH_{α/r}(X, Z) of [LMS14], and drop "the preimage of N(X) by T_{−α/r}".
sourceIssues.reason: With T_{−α/r}(x) = x ∪ e^{−α/r} and e^{−α/r} = (1, −α/r, α²/(2r²)), one computes T_{−α/r}(ar, D + aα, cω) = (ar, D, (c − (α·D)/r − aα²/(2r))ω). Its last coordinate is not an integer in general, for α ∈ H²(X, Z_ℓ(1)) primitive and r = ℓ^n. So the lattice (4.1) is not the preimage of N(X). Lemma 4.2, Proposition 4.3 and §4.2 compute with the explicit lattice (4.1), so the results are unaffected. Noted by the extraction (§4.1 conventions, items 93–106).
